reconcile.note: Gill reads Jesus's question about who touched him as pedagogical, meant to draw the healed woman forward publicly, rather than a genuine admission of ignorance.

discrepancy.note: Strauss finds Jesus's lingering uncertainty over who touched him flatly at odds with the superior knowledge elsewhere ascribed to him.

quotes.text: Accordingly, in the propagation of this history, there was a continual effort to make the result follow immediately on the touch, and to represent Jesus as remaining, even after the cure, for some time uncertain with respect to the individual who had touched him, a circumstance which is in contradiction with that superior knowledge elsewhere attributed to Jesus.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), § 100, on Mark 5:30.

sides.verseText: Immediately Jesus, perceiving in himself that the power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd, and asked, \"Who touched my clothes?\"

sides.snippet: Now we know that you know all things, and don't need for anyone to question you.
sides.verseText: Now we know that you know all things, and don't need for anyone to question you. By this we believe that you came forth from God.\"
